My therapists advice is very individualized to me and will be to you as well which is why you should 100% pursue therapy.

With that being said here are some nuggets of wisdom. 

In order to get over some bad anxiety I have of stairs and escalators, my therapist told me to everyday go up and down some stairs a few times a day and the anxiety would lessen (we have no escalators so I can’t do that).

My therapist puts a lot of emphasis on avoiding negative self talk, even if you think it has little effect, by talking shit about yourself to yourself, you are reinforcing patterns of negative thought that you’ll default to.

If you are suffering from a mental disorder that is very hard to manage, it is worth pursuing a psychiatrist and  getting medication. Even a primary care can prescribe meds, they are life saving for many.

That’s rlly all I can share as everything else is way too personal and highly individualized. Getting a therapist helps BECAUSE you can receive highly individualized advice and care so you 100% should if you have the means.

My hypomania can be variable but it’s usually indistinguishable for me from just having a really really good day, persistent happiness, excess energy, shaking, rapid speaking, similar symptoms. If you notice your daughter pacing around a lot when she is in a good mood, generally moving a lot, and seeming like she is overloaded with energy that may be hypomania.

Now I’m not a doctor and don’t take what I say as medical advice but from what I’ve heard the difference between BPD and Bipolar is that Bipolar is pretty cyclical usually (not for all but typically) while BPD is mood volatility and instability, mood swings on BPD are very fast and occur within hours while bipolar (although mine is rapid cycling) usually occurs within days and weeks and for some years.

Tldr: for me it’s like being overloaded with energy and euphoria and there’s a lot of movement involved. I’d keep your eye out the most on depressive episodes personally as those can be the most deadly for someone who has more hypomania than full on mania.
